name: Piedicavallo Tarocchi
description: Piedicavallo Tarocchi is a rare and highly localized variant of Italian Tarot played exclusively in the Valle Cervo of the Piedmont region. It uses a modified 62-card 'Tarocco Piemontese' deck. The game is famous for its 'Open Communication' system, where partners are legally allowed to speak to each other and signal their cards (using taps and code words) as long as the information is audible to the opponents. It is a game of deep tactical coordination, memory, and traditional heritage.

history.origins: Rooted in the 15th-century tradition of Tarot (Tarocchi), specifically the Piedmontese branch. Piedicavallo developed its own dialect and rule-variants due to its isolation in the Alpine valleys.
timeline: 1700s: Standard Tarocco Piemontese rules circulate in Turin.
1800s: Piedicavallo valley residents adapt the deck to 62 cards (removing specific low suits).
1970s: The 'Communal Talk' rules are documented as a unique cultural asset.
Present: Designated as a UNESCO Intangible Heritage activity in the Biella province.
history.cultural: Played in local cafes (osterie) with a specific Piedmontese vocabulary (e.g., 'Batto' for 'I have the high card').
history.evolution: The game removed several low-rank 'Scartini' (cards of little value) to speed up play and focus on the power of the Trumps (Tarocchi).

setup.players: 4 players in two teams. Partners sit opposite.
setup.deck: 62 cards (22 trumps + 40 suit cards). Low cards (1-4 Swords/Batons, 7-10 Cups/Coins) are removed.
setup.dealing: Dealer gets 17 cards, others 15 cards. The dealer discards 2 cards face-down (the 'Scarto').

rules.objective: Score 57 or more points from a pool of 114 available points.
rules.gameplay: Four players in fixed partnerships (partners opposite) play four deals anticlockwise. Each deal: dealer gives 15 cards to the player to his right, 15 to partner, 15 to the player to his left, and 17 to himself; dealer then discards two cards face-down (scarto). Player to dealer's right leads to the first trick. Follow suit if possible; if not, play a trump if possible; otherwise play any card. Trick with trumps is won by highest trump; trick without trumps by highest card of led suit. Winner of each trick leads to the next. The Fool may be played to any trick and never wins; it is added to the team of whoever played it. Team with more than 57 of the 114 points over the four deals wins the game.
keyRules: Follow suit if possible; if void in suit led, must play a trump if possible.
Fool may be played to any trick; it never wins and is not captured; it counts for the team of the player who played it.
Dealer may not discard 5-point cards (Kings, Trump 21, Trump 1, Fool).
57 or more points of 114 wins a deal; team ahead on total points after four deals wins the game.
Partners may communicate about their cards and tactics within defined limits (open communication).

strategy.basic: Prioritize the protection of the 'Bagatto' (Trump 1). It is worth 5 points but is easily captured. Use the 'Matto' (Fool) to save a high card from a trick you know your partner will win anyway. If you are the dealer, discard useless low numbers into your 'Scarto' to ensure your team captures those 1-point cards early.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Public Signal': When your partner leads a suit, if you have the King, tap the table once. This tells them they don't need to waste a Trump. If you have the Ace, you might use the code word 'Batto' to signal that you will take control of the round. Remember, the opponents hear this tooâ€”use it to intimidate them into playing their low trumps early.
strategy.advanced: Trump Exhaustion: Because there are 21 trumps, you must track which ones have been played. If the 21 and 20 are gone, the 19 becomes the 'King' of the board. Coordination is key: if one partner has high trumps, the other should feed them 'Counters' (10s and face cards) to maximize the point yield from those winning tricks.
tips: If you win all tricks (Vola), the payout is doubled.
Don't discard 5-point cards! It's illegal in most variants unless you have no other choice.

variations.name: Tournament pick-up
variations.description: In tournament play, players other than the dealer may not pick up their cards until after the dealer has discarded.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Timing of card pickup only; no engine constant overrides.

variations.name: Informal pick-up
variations.description: In informal games, players usually pick up and sort their cards as soon as they are dealt, before the dealer discards.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Timing of card pickup only; no engine constant overrides.

variations.name: Tie break
variations.description: If the result is a tie after four deals, two more deals are played to decide the winner.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Extra deals to break tie; no engine overrides for base build.
